newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel reconsiders closing Palestinian offices.
newsitem.headline: Israel reconsiders closing Palestinian offices.

text.p: Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani said on Thursday that Israel was reconsidering its orders to close four Palestinian offices in East Jerusalem.

He said Palestinian officials had promised in writing that the offices had no connection to Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority. "We must examine this thing," he said. "It could be my purpose was achieved."

Israeli police this month issued closure orders to four Palestinian offices in East Jerusalem, saying they were run by the Palestinian Authority. Kahalani was due to discuss the issue with other Israeli officials on Thursday.
Israel says offices working under the Palestinian Authority, which runs self-rule areas in other parts of the West Bank and in the Gaza Strip, are barred from Jerusalem under interim peace deals.
Palestinians deny the offices are linked to the Palestinian Authority, insisting that the closure orders were part of an Israeli intimidation campaign.

The status of Jerusalem is up for negotiation at final peace talks due to begin next week. Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed it. Palestinians want it as capital of a future state.
